text: I gave up my seat to a blind person on the bus. That’s how I lost my job as a bus driver.
gist: Speaker gave up his seat on the bus to a blind person, revealing he was the driver and lost his job.

text: A man on one side of a river shouts to a man standing on the other side, “Hey, how do I get to the other side of the river?” The other man responds, “You are on the other side of the river.”
gist: A man asks someone across a river how to get to the other side and is told he is already on the other side.

text: I said to my wife, "They say that childbirth is the most painful thing someone can experience..." "Now, maybe I was too young to remember, but I didn't think it hurt that much."
gist: Husband dismisses childbirth pain because, as the baby being born, he didn't find it that bad.

text: I was on the phone with my wife and said, "I'm almost home, honey, please put the coffee maker on." After a twenty second pause, I asked, "You still there sweetheart?" "Yeah…" she replied. "But I don't think the coffee maker wants to talk right now…"
gist: Husband asks wife on the phone to put the coffee maker on, and she takes it as handing the coffee maker the phone.

wordplay.explanation: 'put the coffee maker on' as switching it on versus putting it on the phone line.

adaptNote: needs a phrase meaning both switch on and put on the line

gist: Sun forgets his wallet at a coffee shop and the Moon offers to cover him, meaning both paying and an eclipse.

text: Dad, why do scuba divers roll backwards off the boat? Because, son, if they rolled forwards they'd still be in the boat.
gist: Son asks why scuba divers roll backward off boats and dad explains that rolling forward would land them in the boat.

text: My wife sighed, "Why does everything have to be a game with you?" "An excellent question sweetheart!" I said. "But next time, please use the buzzer!"
gist: Wife complains that her husband turns everything into a game, and he praises her question like a quiz host and asks her to use the buzzer next time.
